claim: Replacing the canonical G04 delimiter inverse's rectangular-prefix/ragged-tail reconstruction with a block/active-row strided-slice reconstruction preserves exact bytes but recovers only a narrow amount of inverse wall time on neutral_hostile_v1/09_ml_artifacts.

decision.reason: The candidate is exact and repeatably faster, but it leaves the same 45,979 per-segment bytearray ownership model in place and saves only about 7.15 ms from a roughly 137 ms inverse. Even under the generous assumption that the full microbenchmark saving transfers additively to the prior 243.56 ms policy-verification measurement, the upper-bound whole-policy improvement is only about 2.94%. The result therefore narrows the causal owner: loop/block scheduling is not the dominant remaining opportunity.
decision.next_question: Does eliminating per-segment Python buffers entirely—reconstructing into one contiguous logical output with a native/vectorized scatter—recover a materially larger share of the delimiter inverse cost while preserving exact bytes and existing resource bounds?

scope: One-record, one-workload research oracle. The projected whole-policy reduction is a derived upper bound, not measured product evidence.
